To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) TIMES(0) is an excellent (1)H homodecoupling sequence for ultrafast MAS, (ii), the sensitivity of (1)J-HMQC is greatly enhanced when the decoupled (1)H spins are in a rigid environment and (iii) TIMES(0)-based (1)JHMQC is an excellent tool for the characterization of (13)C chemical shifts and (1)H/(13)C through-bond J couplings

(1)H decouple-HMQC measurements with TIMES(0) at ν(r)=60 and 80kHz MAS provide a sensitivity gain of 2.3 to 4.0 compared with (1)D-HMQC measurements at ν(r)=20kHz MAS and that (2) the TIMES(0) scheme is a very efficient tool to obtain (1)H chemical shifts of protons in organic molecules with high sensitivity and good resolution.

the TIMES(0) (Tilted Magic Echo Sandwich with zero degree Sandwich pulse) sequence is a very efficient homonuclear decoupling scheme that can be used for (1)J-coupling measurements in (1)J-HMQC experiments at very fast MAS.

the TIMES(0) is the best choice for (1) H-{(1)H} decoupled (1)H-HMQC experiments in combination with (1) H-detected (1)H-((13)C) correlation measurements at ultra-fast MAS.
TIMES(0) provides the most efficient (1)H decouping for through-bond (1)H-HMQC experiments at very fast MAS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the TIMES(0) pulse sequence is an attractive choice for (1) H-{X} Heteronuclear Multiple Quantum Coherence experiments in combination with fast Magic-Angle Spinning.
TIMES(0) is the most suitable scheme to be used in (1) H-(X) HMQC experiments, in which (1)H is the indirect detection nucleus and (X) the direct detection nucleus, at ultra-fast MAS.

TIMES(0) is the best sequence for (1) H-(1)H heteronuclear dipolar recoupling at ultra-fast MAS and that the TIMES(0) scheme can be used in (1) H-{(13) C} through-bond HMQC measurements with a sensitivity comparable to the best through-space HMQC schemes, but with much better performance in terms of t(1)- and t(2)-noise.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the TIMES(0) scheme can be used as an alternative for through-space (1)H decoup- ling in J-HMQC measurements, and is a good candidate for the (1)H- (1)H homodimensional (1)H-HMQC measurements at very fast (1)H MAS rates.
(1)H-1H decoupling in (1) H-(1)H J-HMQC is a viable approach to measure long-range (1)H-C(1) connectivities in proteins at ultra-fast MAS.
